title: Degree-one Cech cohomology of a line bundle is independent of a two-affine cover
author: @tomasz
source: Consequence of Stacks Project, Lemma 30.2.6, Tag 01XD (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XD), applied to each of the two covers and to the quasi-coherent invertible sheaf M. The source identifies affine-cover Cech cohomology with sheaf cohomology as modules over global functions. Compose the two comparisons in degree one and restrict scalars along R -> Gamma(X,O_X). For a two-open cover, the normalized degree-one Cech module is the cokernel of the difference of restrictions. The covers explicitly include affine intersections, so no additional separatedness assumption is needed. This states cover independence, not a literal transcription of the source.

title: Lifting curve tests through proper surjections with positive degree
author: @tomasz
source: Derived multisection consequence: choose a closed point of the generic fibre of Y times_X C and normalize its reduced closure. Stacks Project, Theorem 53.2.6 and Lemma 53.2.8 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BXX) provide the normal projective curve and smoothness over a perfect field; Lemma 53.2.4 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CCL) gives finiteness of the nonconstant map. The simultaneous degree identity is Lemma 33.44.11 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AYZ), with degree defined by Definition 33.44.1. The charts are two affine opens on a smooth proper curve. This combines these standard facts rather than asserting a verbatim source theorem.

title: Restriction differences for an invertible sheaf are surjective on an affine union
author: @tomasz
source: Consequence of Stacks Project, Lemma 30.2.2, Tag 01XB (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XB), and the Mayer-Vietoris sequence, Lemma 20.8.2, Tag 01EB (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01EB). Restrict the invertible, hence quasi-coherent, sheaf to the affine open W = U union V. Affine vanishing gives H^1(W,M) = 0. Exactness of Mayer-Vietoris then makes the difference of section restrictions onto Gamma(U intersection V,M). Reversing the source convention for the sign preserves surjectivity. The two component opens and their intersection need not be affine. This is a consequence in terms of sections, not a literal transcription of either cited lemma.

title: A finite multisection of a proper surjection onto a smooth curve
author: @tomasz
source: Derived normalized-multisection consequence of the Stacks Project: normalization of varieties, Lemma 33.27.1 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BXR); normal proper models of curve function fields, Theorem 53.2.6 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BY1); smoothness over a perfect field, Lemma 53.2.8 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BY3); and finiteness of nonconstant maps of proper curves, Lemma 53.2.4 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CCL). Choose a closed point of the nonempty generic fibre of p, take its reduced closure, and normalize. Its residue field is finite over K(C), so the closure has dimension one. Properness and dominance give a surjective curve map. Algebraically closed K is perfect. This states the resulting multisection consequence, not a verbatim transcription of any one lemma.

title: Finitely many smooth-curve degrees detect numerical triviality
author: @tomasz

This is the explicitly conditional construction in that proof: the finite injective immersion and proper smooth function are supplied as hypotheses. Positivity of the proper function is unnecessary because the compact-preimage estimate bounds its absolute value. The bounded diffeomorphism is x/sqrt(1+norm(x)^2), as in Mathlib OpenPartialHomeomorph.univUnitBall; the source PDF p.6 displays x/(1+norm(x)^2), which is not injective as written. The formalization uses the corrected standard smooth compression x/sqrt(1+norm(x)^2). The PDF page was visually checked.
